topSignals.title: AEP + Bloom Energy 1 GW deal: $2,944/kW bundled — first utility-scale EaaS benchmark (first full coverage)
topSignals.text: — The January 8, 2026 agreement (referenced in the pipeline list but never fully analyzed) has AEP purchasing up to 1 GW of Bloom SOFCs for AI data centers across its service territory, with an initial 100 MW order. The total commitment of $2.65B for ~900 MW implies an all-in bundled cost of ~$2,944/kW — inclusive of capital equipment, 20-year service, and reportedly maintenance (fuel procurement is likely separate at AEP's utility scale). This is dramatically below individual-project capex of $6,639–7,224/kW and represents the first public market reference for large-volume utility-purchase pricing. A separately reported PPA rate from Bloom EaaS deployments (Enkiai/Electron Economics) comes in at ~$0.10/kWh, a premium over grid power ($0.06–0.08/kWh) reflecting the time-to-power and location advantage. DCD | AEP press release | Fuel Cells Works | Enkiai EaaS pricing

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy rebounds +9.6% to ~$312 on first post-holiday session
topSignals.text: — BE opened Monday July 6 trading with strong buying interest, recovering from the $270 trough reached on the July 3 pre-holiday shortened session. The holiday weekend cleared the residual selling pressure from the June 26 Russell reconstitution event ($309 → $252) and the shortened July 3 session ($299 → $271). At ~$312, BE sits between the Wells Fargo bear case ($217) and the UBS/Evercore Outperform dual target ($350), with Q2 earnings on July 30 as the next major catalyst. Consensus remains ~$820M Q2 revenue / ~34% gross margin / EPS ~$0.39. stockanalysis.com | Motley Fool H2 preview

topSignals.title: Renewable PPA prices hit multi-year highs — "renewables + firming" model gets more expensive
topSignals.text: — Per LevelTen's Q1 2026 PPA Price Index, North American wind PPAs averaged $79.40/MWh (+24% YoY) and solar $64.49/MWh (+13% YoY) — the highest reported rates since 2018. The rising cost of the primary competing model for AI data center power (variable renewables + gas firming, as deployed by Google at Meitner Energy Center) narrows the all-in LCOE gap vs. SOFC. SOFC baseload remains costlier in absolute terms ($130–225/MWh LCOE range), but the benchmark gap is shrinking. LevelTen PPA Index / Utility Dive

items.text: Post-EFCF results still dark — As of July 6, no technical results from the 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum (closed July 3, Lucerne) have been published online. Proceedings distributed on USB sticks to participants; public press releases from Elcogen, Ceres Power, SolydEra, and Convion expected this week. This remains the highest-priority pending data item for the LCOE model. Key watch: Elcogen E3000 G2 real-commercial efficiency at 650°C (stated 75% electrical / 90% CHP), Doosan yield trajectory beyond Q1 2026's 80%. EFCF

AEP 1 GW deployment details (first full coverage) — See Top Signal #1. AEP's utility footprint covers 11 US states (Ohio, West Virginia, Texas, Oklahoma, Indiana, Michigan, Virginia, Tennessee, Arkansas, Louisiana, Kentucky). Announced 20% annual commercial load growth expected over the next three years, driven entirely by data center development — the largest utility fuel cell initiative in US history. Initial 100 MW order underway; expansion to 900 MW–1 GW anticipated. The SOFC units are deployed behind-the-meter at co-located AI data center sites. AEP / StockTitan

Quiet otherwise. Active pipeline: Oracle/Jupiter 2.45 GW, Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW initial H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW, AEP/Bloom 1 GW, Bloom/Brookfield $25B, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

Renewable PPA cost escalation — See Top Signal #3. The Google Meitner Energy Center template (wind/solar + gas firming, Texas Panhandle) is becoming more expensive as PPA prices rise. At $79.40/MWh wind + $64.49/MWh solar + gas firming premium, the "clean-energy-first" model no longer has as stark a cost advantage over SOFC at data-center scale. SOFC still loses on absolute LCOE ($130–225/MWh vs. $64–80/MWh renewables) but the delta is compressing.

Quiet otherwise. Microsoft Project Kilby (2.67 GW CCGT, Texas, first power 2028), DOE $17.5B AP1000 nuclear loan programme, and three zero-power microreactor criticalities (July 3) remain the competitive backdrop with no updates.

Bloom Energy (BE) — Holiday-return bounce to ~$312 (+9.6%); range ~$290–320 intraday. Analyst picture unchanged (seven analysts): WF $217 EW | Barclays $276 EW | Roth Capital $285 Neutral | Clear Street $290 | RBC $335 OP | UBS $350 Buy | Evercore ISI $350 OP. Structural concerns: 34% share dilution in two quarters, persistent negative margins, S-3ASR shelf registration + 12M Fit Energy warrants. Analyst: B. Riley Buy $32 | Jefferies Buy $24 | UBS Neutral $22. Q3 FY2026 earnings ~September 2026. Yahoo Finance | TipRanks comparison
Post-EFCF: no results published yet — As of July 6 (Monday after close July 3). Watch elcogen.com, ceres.tech, solydera.com, and convion.fi press release channels this week.

Wiley / Chemical Reviews (ACS) comprehensive SOFC modeling review — "A Comprehensive Review of Modeling of Solid Oxide Fuel Cells: From Large Systems to Fine Electrodes" (ACS Chemical Reviews, 2024/2025) — covers multiscale simulation approaches from system-level to electrode-scale; benchmark reference for SOFC degradation and performance modeling. Useful context for LCOE uncertainty quantification. ACS ChemRev

NCBi/PMC special issue: "Materials Frontiers for SOFCs: Structure-Performance Correlation" — Editorial for SI covering electrode-electrolyte interfaces, chromium poisoning, and novel cathode compositions. Companion to the PMC 50,000h lifetime modeling paper (covered June 28). NCBi PMC

lcoe.text: AEP bundled benchmark: $2,944/kW over 20 years (capital + service, fuel likely separate) — At utility purchase scale (900 MW–1 GW), Bloom prices equipment+service at $2,944/kW — approximately 55–60% below individual-project capex of $6,639–7,224/kW. This is the first confirmed large-volume utility pricing benchmark. Recommend adding a "utility-scale purchase" scenario to the LCOE model with $2,944/kW as the capex+service proxy, then adding fuel cost separately at $5/MMBtu and $8/MMBtu. DCD / AEP | Fuel Cells Works

Bloom EaaS power price: ~$0.10/kWh — First market reference for the bundled $/MWh rate Bloom charges data center customers under Energy-as-a-Service contracts. At $0.10/kWh = $100/MWh: this is at the low end of the $130–225/MWh LCOE range in the model, suggesting Bloom is accepting lower margins to accelerate deployment, OR the full-service bundle reflects lower capex at scale. Premium over grid ($60–80/MWh) is the "time-to-power" and "grid-bypass" value capture. Enkiai

Wind PPA: $79.40/MWh (+24% YoY); Solar PPA: $64.49/MWh (+13% YoY) — New benchmarks for the competing renewables model. At $79.40/MWh wind with gas firming (~$15–25/MWh premium), the "clean energy + firming" total delivered cost reaches ~$95–105/MWh — approaching Bloom's EaaS $100/MWh rate. The cost advantage of the renewables-first model over SOFC is narrowing materially. Use $79.40/MWh wind and $64.49/MWh solar as updated PPA benchmarks in the LCOE model competing scenario. LevelTen / Utility Dive

Q2 earnings July 30 remains the primary model update trigger: manufacturing cost per kW at 2 GW Fremont run rate, product gross margin, any EaaS pricing disclosure from Nebius or Brookfield-financed deployments.
